macro.text: Nvidia −5.2% premarket after its board opened an independent probe into reports CEO Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort; earnings Nov 17.

Oil: WTI 87.63 (−3.5%), Brent 94.30 (−4.1%). Tehran proposed cutting the talks restart timetable to two days; Rubio calls its demands 'outrageous'; Trump says new strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress.
Bonds: 10-year 4.859% and 30-year 5.260% (Friday close); Goldman says the 10-year could settle in a 4.75–5.0% range if risk assets calm. Dollar index 101.85 (−0.4%), gold 4,129.40 (+1.3%).
Citi cut US equities and global tech to neutral on AI positioning risk, and raised global health care to overweight.
Fed: December 9 hike odds near 70–80% after hot payrolls; Bowman and Barkin speak today; October CPI Tue 8:30 (0.3% m/m, core 0.2%), PPI Fri.
China's October producer prices rose 5.7% vs 5.3% expected, the highest in over four years; consumer prices 0.7% vs 0.8%.

flowNote: Money is going into the broad, cost- and rate-sensitive market as oil falls: industrials (XLI +1.4%), materials (XLB +1.4%), consumer discretionary (XLY +1.3%), small caps (IWM +1.2%) and health care (XLV +1.2%, helped by Citi's upgrade). In AI, it is going to contracted power (CEG's beat; NRG +4.8%) and the hyperscalers (AMZN +3.0%). It is leaving energy (XLE −0.6% with Brent −4%) and semiconductors (SMH −0.2%, Nvidia −5.5%), while tech (XLK +0.3%) and software (IGV +0.4%) lag the index.

focus: Nvidia −5.5% premarket (176.47) as its board probes CEO Huang's tie to an alleged spy
Futures up on cheaper oil: Dow +~500 pts, SPY +0.7%, IWM +1.2%; Brent −4.1% to 94.30
Constellation beats and raises: adj. EPS $5.06 vs $3.89; 2026 guide $12.50–12.80
AI power bid on CEG: NRG +4.8%, GEV +2.6%, ETN +2.1%, PWR +2.1%, VRT +1.9%
Hyperscalers up: AMZN +3.0%, META +2.6%, GOOGL +2.5%, MSFT +2.1%; AMD +3.3% on upgrade
CPI tomorrow 8:30 (core 0.2% expected) and CoreWeave after the close; no red events today
bigPicture: The market is rewarding owners of built capacity and contracted power (hyperscalers, CEG) and still punishing the leveraged AI tail and anything with headline risk (NVDA, CRWV).
Cheaper oil (Brent −4% on Iran talk-timetable headlines) is lifting the broad, rate- and cost-sensitive market: industrials, materials, discretionary and small caps lead premarket.
Wall Street is turning cautious on positioning, not demand: Citi cut US equities to neutral on AI sentiment and moved global health care to overweight.
Rates still cap any rebound: December hike odds sit near 70–80% (report), and Tuesday's CPI is the last before the Dec 9 meeting.
snapshot.takeaway: A broad, oil-driven bounce with Nvidia as the exception and no data today. The tape is paying for contracted power and hyperscalers, not for the leveraged AI tail; with CPI and CoreWeave tomorrow, let the first 15 minutes show whether gaps like CEG's (already faded from 263) and NRG's hold before trusting them.

WTI −3.5% to 87.63 and Brent −4.1% to 94.30 after Tehran proposed a two-day timetable to restart talks and Trump called renewed strikes 'highly unlikely' if talks progress, though Rubio sees no breakthrough. XLE −0.6% premarket, −12% over 5 days; Occidental reports after the close.
